newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Crown fluctuations no obstacle to EMU - Sweden.
newsitem.headline: Crown fluctuations no obstacle to EMU - Sweden.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Friday that recent crown fluctuations were not a hindrance for membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
Asbrink reiterated his position that linking the crown to Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) was not on the agenda.

"If it is allowed for the currency to fluctuate plus or minus 15 percent within ERM, the Swedish currency keeps very well within that interval," Asbrink told journalists after a meeting with the Swedish parliament's EU committee.
Sweden argues that EMU membership merely requires a stable currency, not ERM membership. The crown has softened 7.5 percent against the mark since October.

"We have seen a softening in the crown since October," Asbrink said. "We are not ignoring that problem. But with our currency exchange criteria we have not pledged to have a fixed exchange rate so there is room for fluctuations."
"But I'm not unconcerned about currency fluctuations," he added.
Sweden's minority Social Democratic government has still not revealed whether it is for or against EMU membership, saying a party congress will decide this autumn.
